name: OmniQuant (learnable weight clipping + equivalent transformation)
bits: reported at w2a16, w3a16, w4a16, w4a4, w6a6 and w8a8 (paper enumerates these configurations)
activation_scheme: Learnable Equivalent Transformation (LET) folds an activation-only affine transform into the adjacent weights so activation outliers are handled without changing the network function in full precision; Learnable Weight Clipping (LWC) optimizes the per-tensor clipping threshold. Both are optimized by block-wise error minimization over 128 calibration samples - hence OmniQuant is a PTQ/calibration method, not data-free.
kernels: Research-only; no shipping kernel in the paper.
quality_delta: Paper states LLaMA-2 7B-70B is processed within 1-16 hours on a single A100-40G using 128 samples, and validates across w2a16/w3a16/w4a16/w4a4/w6a6 without naming a headline accuracy number in the abstract. No numeric quality delta recorded.
notes: Enum mismatch: 'smoothquant' is the nearest existing value because LET is structurally the same idea as SmoothQuant - an offline, calibration-driven migration of quantization difficulty from activations into weights that leaves full-precision behaviour unchanged. The difference is that SmoothQuant's migration parameter alpha is hand-chosen per layer while OmniQuant learns it. Request the parent add 'omniquant'. Worth keeping separate from smoothquant because OmniQuant is the standard W2A16/W3A16 baseline: those low-bit weight-only configurations collapse under round-to-nearest and OmniQuant is one of the few PTQ methods that survives them. SCHEME RECLASSIFIED (parent agent, 2026-10-03): scheme was 'smoothquant' (a proxy recorded while the enum lacked a legal value) and is now 'omniquant'.
